subject: Renewal: TerraForge capacity uplift — proposed stabilizer & commit options
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@terraforge.ai>, procurement@terraforge.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: TerraForge capacity uplift — initial context and tracker

Hi Asha / procurement team,

Thanks again for the time last week. Your renewal window comes up in ~45 days and I wanted to get a short, practical thread going to align on capacity and economics before we route paperwork. Key facts from our end: your average monthly token consumption is up ~2.5x YoY and your Q3 forecast pins a further 30% growth with the new vector search use case.

Attached: SOW_v3_TerraForge.pdf (proposed scope) and TerraForge_MA_Pricing_Tracker.xlsx (current usage + baseline).

From a negotiation standpoint, we typically see two levers that help customers with growth while preserving unit economics for both sides: 1) short-term price stabilizer/price-cap while you scale to committed levels, and 2) structured uplift credits that soften early overage impact as commits ramp.

Can you confirm: expected committed throughput for next 12 months (low/likely/high), and constraints on PO timing (do you need a signed SOW + PO before Aug 15)? That will determine whether we propose an invoice-timing concession or a temporary bridge credit.

Happy to set up 30m next week if that helps.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
(irene@redwood.com)

--
Attachments: SOW_v3_TerraForge.pdf, TerraForge_MA_Pricing_Tracker.xlsx

From: Asha Patel <asha@terraforge.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@terraforge.ai, Mark Greenwood <m.greenwood@terraforge.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: TerraForge capacity uplift — initial context and tracker

Hi Irene — thanks for the summary and the tracker.

A few quick constraints from our side:
- Procurement needs price stability for the first 6 months post-renewal to accommodate customer pilots. A six-month price hold would materially help our finance team.
- We can commit to a 20% uplift in committed throughput this quarter with a path to 50% within 6 months, but that hinges on having predictable unit pricing and a PO cadence that aligns with our revenue recognition (we usually run on net60).
- Overages are a concern for us: would Redwood consider a credit buffer (applied to the next invoice) for the first two months if actual usage exceeds the new commit?

I've looped in Mark (legal) and procurement so they can speak to contract language and PO timing. Please also include any proposed SLA adjustments for the scaling period.

Asha Patel
VP Product, TerraForge AI
asha@terraforge.ai

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: TerraForge renewal — Asha asks for 6mo price hold + two-month overage buffer

Karthik / Jordan — forwarding Asha's reply and the tracker. Quick ask: can you each weigh in on feasibility and appetite for the following proposed options (we'll present these to TerraForge on Friday if possible):

Option A — Accelerated commit + temporary price hold
- Commit: +30% baseline for 12 months
- Price: current unit price held for first 6 months, then 6% step-up after month 6 if usage < committed level
- Credits: 2 months of overage credits (capped at 25% of monthly invoice) to be applied to next invoice
- Invoice terms: net60 (no change)
- Margin / finance note: require Karthik to confirm blended margin impact (we'd be subsidizing short-term to get long-term commit).

Option B — Phased commit with uplift credits
- Commit: +20% quarter 1, additional +30% locked in by month 6 (conditional on milestone usage)
- Price: 4% discount on committed units for 12 months; no price hold beyond month 1
- Credits: pro-rated credits for month-over-month overages during ramp (month 1-3)
- Invoice terms: prefer net30 for Redwood cashflow; customer asks net60 — need Ben's input on whether finance can accept net60 for this deal size.

Option C — No commit increase, bridge protection
- Commit stays flat; Redwood provides a 6-month bridge price-cap (no increases) and 3 months of credits for overage. Higher unit price thereafter. Good if TerraForge can't sign higher commit today.

Questions:
1) Karthik — blended margin impact and acceptable credit ceiling for option A and C?
2) Jordan — any legal flags on a temporary price-hold clause and the exact language for credit application?
3) Ben — can finance accept net60 on the signed SOW if we provide the credits & 6mo price-stabilizer?

If we agree internally I'll draft a single-page options memo to send to Asha and Mark.

Thanks,
Irene

--

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@terraforge.ai>, procurement@terraforge.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: three-path offer for TerraForge renewal (price-cap + ramp credits)

Hi Asha / Mark — thanks for the quick turn. Per our internal review we landed on three concrete paths. Pick the one that best matches your procurement timeline; we'll convert to SOW + DocuSign once you confirm.

Option 1 — Growth Accelerator (recommended)
- Commit: +35% baseline (12-mo term)
- Pricing: current unit price held for 6 months (price-cap), then 4% uplift months 7-12
- Credits: two-month overage credit pool equal to up to 20% of each monthly invoice during months 1-2 of the term
- Invoice: net60 allowed (we'll accept PO aligned to your revenue timing)
- Implementation: Redwood will prioritize onboarding via Dedicated pool for first 90 days to keep latency stable

Option 2 — Phased Ramp (balanced)
- Commit: +20% immediately, additional +25% locked as milestone at month 3
- Pricing: 4% discount on committed units for 12 months, no extended price hold
- Credits: pro-rated month-over-month credits during ramp (months 1-3)
- Invoice: net30 preferred by Redwood; if TerraForge requires net60, finance asks for a 15% early-payment accelerator to offset working capital

Option 3 — Bridge Guard (conservative)
- Commit: no increase at sign
- Pricing: 6-month price-cap; higher unit price thereafter if commit doesn't increase
- Credits: 3 months of overage credits (smaller cap than option 1)
- Invoice: net60 or split PO schedule (2x invoices)

Two operational notes:
- Legal language: Jordan will draft a 6-month "stabilizer" clause that explicitly states the temporary price cap and the mechanics for credit application (credits are applied to the following invoice, cannot be rolled past month 3).
- Finance: Ben confirms we can accept net60 for Option 1 with the credit structure; he'll put the final note on the SOW.

Next steps: please confirm preferred option by EOB Jul 25 and we will push a DocuSign-ready SOW. I included the DocuSign pre-fill link here: https://www.docusign.com/terraforge-renewal-link-DF20892 and the HubSpot deal for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/DF-2027-0892

If you'd like a short call to run the numbers live I'm available Wed/Thu next week.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com
